name: machine0
caveats: List prices; CPU sizes regular/shared, NVMe and dedicated premium differ. Marketing headline dedicated resources does not mean all vCPUs dedicated.
Monthly figures are illustrative, not a price cap; per-minute billing. $5 minimum refundable top-up. GPU bundle prices include CPU/RAM; do not treat them as GPU-only add-ons.
Suspending stops compute; image storage is $0.078/GB-month. Snapshot is disk-based unless memory preservation verified.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Bandwidth: $0.01/GiB beyond a "1-10 TB free allowance per size" (per-size split not published; card uses 1 TB). Machines are billed while running AND stopped; only suspend stops compute billing. No desktop/browser product: a GUI or headless browser must be installed by you on the VM.
Machines are auto-suspended when the prepaid balance drops to a suspension threshold (estimated snapshot/image/disk storage for the 7-day retention period), not at zero.

fleet.verification: First prepaid top-up unlocks paid concurrency; homepage minimum top-up $5. Additional ID/KYC not documented.
fleet.tiers: Free 1 until first top-up; new paid signups 50 concurrent since July 28, 2026. Existing accounts retain prior limits.
fleet.notes: Official changelog corrects old new-account cap of 3 to 50, while retaining free limit 1. 10/50 need first top-up; 300/1,000 higher quota procedure not stated. API request-rate increases are separate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: **Suspend** snapshots the VM, deletes the cloud instance, and stops machine billing.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: the suspend command (the snapshot 'suspended-<machine>-<date>-<time>' is taken automatically and restored on `machine0 start`), and automatic suspension when the prepaid balance hits the suspension threshold (changelog 1.0.166: 'Machines are auto-suspended when your balance drops to a suspension threshold'). Plain `stop` does not snapshot. No idle-timeout auto-suspend documented. Disk only (DigitalOcean-backed snapshot; VM gets a new IP, memory preservation not documented).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshot a VM into a reusable image. The VM is stopped automatically before snapshotting.
snapshot_on_demand.note: `machine0 images new <vm> <image>` (also MCP images tools); disk only, VM is stopped first (no live/memory snapshot). New machines boot from it (`machine0 new clone --image my-image`); images are versioned. $0.078/GB-month.

harness_api.quote: Gives agents the same capabilities as the CLI.
harness_api.note: API surface = CLI + remote MCP (machines, images, SSH keys, ssh_exec, sizes). Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode are preinstalled and profiles pre-authenticate them and serve prompts/MCPs, but you SSH in and run `claude` yourself; no API to start an agent with a prompt, stream its events or resume conversations.

ingress_rules.quote: HTTPS endpoints at `<vm>.mac0.io` are authenticated to the VM owner.
ingress_rules.note: Provider-side control is only the owner-authenticated HTTPS proxy (to port 80). The dedicated public IPv4 is filtered only by in-guest ufw (22/80/443 open by default), which is not provider-side; no cloud firewall / IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.quote: All VMs run `ufw` with ports 22, 80, and 443 open.
guest_firewall.note: Full DigitalOcean VM with sudo; ufw enabled by default, open more with `sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp`.

secret_proxy.quote: Injected credentials are plain files on the VM and travel with [snapshots](/platform/images).
secret_proxy.note: Profile secrets and integration credentials (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub, machine0 API key) are written into the VM as env files / credential files (/etc/environment, ~/.claude.json etc.); `--secret` only makes them write-only in the control plane. Profile MCP gateway proxies remote MCP servers (credentials held server-side), but that is MCP only, not HTTP egress injection.

volume_attach.quote: Disks are persistent block storage volumes that live independently of any VM.
volume_attach.note: 10-16384 GB, 5 per VM, 10 per account; attach at create or to a running VM; ~$0.1667/GB-month; not on GPU sizes or NixOS VMs yet.

volume_shared.quote: A disk lives in one region and attaches to one VM at a time.
volume_shared.note: Block volume, read-write, single attach. No shared filesystem documented.
